title: Logical Reasoning with Relation Network for Inductive Knowledge Graph Completion

problem.claim: Inductive knowledge graph completion infers missing relations for newly arriving entities absent from the training set.

gap.claim: Existing inductive methods are limited by data sparsity, cold-start conditions, and the coarse-grained reasoning available from a few neighboring entities.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes NORAN, a relation network for inductive knowledge graph completion.
NORAN mines latent relation patterns for inductive knowledge graph completion.
NORAN centers KG modeling on relations and captures relation correlations as entity-independent logical evidence for inductive completion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe NORAN as a novel relation network for inductive KG completion.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on five benchmarks.
The authors report that NORAN substantially outperforms state-of-the-art knowledge graph completion methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Inductive KGC targets missing relations for new entities, a setting motivated by continuously evolving real-world knowledge graphs; prior work uses message passing over subgraphs.
Prior inductive methods face data sparsity, cold-start conditions, and coarse reasoning from few neighboring entities.
The paper introduces NORAN to mine latent relation patterns through a relation-centered view that captures entity-independent logical evidence.
The authors report substantial performance gains over state-of-the-art methods on five benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Relation correlations can be modeled as entity-independent logical evidence for inductive KGC.

interpretation.claim: Relation-level patterns may complement entity-local information when new entities have sparse neighborhoods.

application.claim: For inductive KGC, consider relation-centered signals when local entity connectivity is limited.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how this approach behaves across other tasks or data conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the five benchmark names, evaluation metrics, or baseline configurations.
The abstract does not describe NORAN's architecture, training procedure, or ablation results.
The abstract does not quantify the reported performance improvements.
